learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge needed to understand the issues relating to transmission of information, and to know how to apply appropriate design procedures of wireless communication systems.
Integrate knowledge gained in previous courses like electromagnetic fields, telecommunications, and signal theory to provide a solid technical background on communication systems.

Correctly interpret the causes of degradation and hindrance to information transmission, and implement appropriate design choices commonly addressed in engineering practice related to wireless communications.
Correctly choose the appropriate transmission medium, and the associated system architecture, to meet the system requirements.
Identify and properly quantify the parameters necessary for the dimensioning of the system.
Identify the causes of performance degradation, and the suitable countermeasures.

Improve the student
’s ability to learn independently and to draw conclusions.

Stimulate and refine the student
’s ability to communicate and independence of judgment through oral discussions.

syllabus_topics: Block diagram of a wireless communication system
Radio channel characteristics, channel models (Flat and Selective fading, time-varying channels)
Spread spectrum and multiple access techniques: Principles of DS-SS and CDMA

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (discussion on topics and solution of a dimensioning problem)

assessment_rules: The learning assessment consists of an oral exam, comprising a discussion on course topics (including lab sessions) and the solution of a dimensioning problem. Some oral questions may require short calculations. The minimum mark for passing the exam is 18/30. The highest rating is achieved by demonstrating a thorough understanding of the course content, exposed with complete appropriateness of technical language. Praise is given to students who perform correctly and completely and demonstrate particular brilliance in oral discussion and exercise solution.
